applicable_when: The kernel is a pointwise fused op (bias-add + mul + tanh + sigmoid) over 110M elements. With XBLOCK=128, the grid has 861,056 blocks each processing only 128 elements. This creates massive launch overhead and each warp has very few in-flight memory operations to hide L1TEX latency (tanh + sigmoid are transcendental ops with high latency). The scheduler shows 45.7% idle cycles with only 0.91 eligible warps/scheduler, and CPIStall reports 9.1 cycles average L1TEX scoreboard wait (59.2% of total stall). Increasing XBLOCK to 1024-2048 reduces grid size by 8-16x, gives each CTA more work to overlap memory latency, improves ILP within a warp, and reduces per-element launch overhead. With only 16 registers/thread there is ample headroom to increase tile size without register spilling.
